text:
maria-new: Hi team, I start on-call rotation next week and hit a couple of onboarding bumps. The runbook link in the welcome email 403s for me. Who owns docs SSO?

owen-sre: Welcome Maria! :wave: That's usually docs-sso. Ping @devops or me with your LDAP username and I'll add you to oncall-readers. Which Pager (A/B) did you get?

maria-new: Pager A per the schedule. Also my PagerDuty mobile push isn't showing alerts — I acknowledged a test from the web UI but the phone didn't buzz.

owen-sre: Two things: confirm PD app notifications allowed on the phone, and ensure your contact method has the mobile number set (PD -> My Profile). If the app still doesn't buzz, check device-level Do Not Disturb or battery optimization. If all looks good, I'll trigger a staging test alert.

maria-new: I checked settings and cleared DND. Still nothing. Could the PD push be blocked by our device management? I'm on a managed laptop + personal phone.

devops: If company MDM blocks push notifications for PD we can't change that; use SMS fallback in PD contacts for now. We can add your phone as SMS contact — send it to me in DM.

maria-new: Sent number via DM. One more: for shadow sessions, should I be taking control (ack, annotate) or just observing? The onboarding doc says "first 2 incidents shadow" but not the role.

owen-sre: Good Q. For first shadow incidents we prefer a guided hands-on: you perform the initial acknowledgement, set severity, and add a short timeline note. We'll be watching and will jump in if things escalate. Don't worry about permanent assignments.

maria-new: Nice. Is there a simulated incident I can run without paging people in prod? I'd like to practice the full flow: ack, follow playbook, run mitigation script, annotate, and resolve.

owen-sre: Use the incident-sim job in staging. It only pages the staging PD schedule and posts to #eng-oncall-staging. Repo: git@github.com:redwood/incident-sim.git. Run locally:```git clone git@github.com:redwood/incident-sim.git
cd incident-sim
./run_sim.sh --env staging --type partial-outage```

docs-bot: Runbook snapshot v2026-04-18 (source: runbooks/oncall). If you see mismatches with handbook open a docs issue.

maria-new: Thanks. Quick question about annotations: what's the preferred format for timeline entries? Any template?

owen-sre: We use short bullet entries with ISO timestamps. Example:```2026-05-05T02:12Z - Alert triggered: high error rate on model inference
2026-05-05T02:15Z - Acknowledged (Pager A) - set severity P2
2026-05-05T02:18Z - Mitigation: scaled inference replicas from 4 to 12 (redwoodctl routing scale --service inference --replicas 12)
2026-05-05T02:27Z - Monitoring: error rate trending down -> resolved```

maria-new: Perfect. One more operational: if I need to escalate to oncall manager (for example, PRNG or compliance P0), what's the path? The runbook mentions "oncall-manager contact" but no direct number.

owen-sre: For managerial escalations use the PD escalation policy which pages the oncall-manager schedule after 15 minutes at P0. If you need immediate contact, DM @owen-sre and I'll call. For compliance-sensitive incidents, email security@redwood and notify via PD with the "security" tag.

oncall-bot: @maria-new added to Pager A schedule for next rotation. Shadow pairing: @owen-sre (Mon 09:00-11:00), @devops (Wed 14:00-15:30).

maria-new: Great, seeing the schedule now. Any last-minute checklist before my first night?

owen-sre: Short checklist: 1) Confirm PD mobile or SMS contact 2) Run incident-sim in staging once 3) Install redwoodctl + kubectl (brew install redwoodctl kubectl) 4) Upload SSH pubkey to infra if you need bastion access 5) Read top-of-runbook severity rubric and paging rules. If you want we'll do a 30m dry run Tue morning.

maria-new: Thank you all, that helps a ton. I'll run the sim and install tools tonight. See you Tue! :thumbsup:
